$comment: What is measured, and where each number comes from in the harness's output. harness/summarize.py and the website both read this file, so a metric means the same thing everywhere it appears. Lower is better for every one.

metrics.title: Open a message
metrics.what: Click a message in the list until the reader has finished drawing it.

metrics.title: Next message
metrics.what: Press ↓ until the next message has finished drawing.

metrics.title: Search
metrics.what: Type a word into the search field until the results have finished drawing. Typing it is part of the time, about 80 ms.

metrics.title: Launch
metrics.what: Open the app until the inbox is on screen and has stopped changing. Warm: the app has run before and its files are cached.

metrics.title: Quit
metrics.what: Ask the app to quit, as the menu item does, until its process has exited. The process is checked every 2 ms.

metrics.title: Scroll
metrics.what: Thirty notches of the scroll wheel until the list stops moving. Posting the thirty notches takes about 240 ms of it.

metrics.title: Memory
metrics.what: Physical footprint after the tests, as Activity Monitor counts it, including the helper processes macOS charges to the app (WebKit, GPU, networking).

metrics.title: Idle CPU
metrics.what: Share of one core used over ten seconds of the app sitting idle after the tests.

metrics.title: First sync
metrics.what: Downloading the whole mailbox into an empty store, measured at the server: from the first busy second to the last. Indexing after the last byte is not included.

metrics.title: Store on disk
metrics.what: Apparent size of the client's local store for the benchmark account. Not like-for-like: clients keep different things (the original message, parsed fields, a search index), so this is listed, never ranked.
